text:
B: Alright! Hello, can you hear me?
A: Yes, hello. Sorry, I'm Joanne.
B: Tendai. How you doing, Joanne? You've done a couple of these now, yeah?
A: Two. I'm still not sure I'm doing it right.
B: Ah, there's no right. It's just a chat, you know. Like at the bus stop.
A: I don't really talk at bus stops.
B: Ha! Me, I talk to everybody. Natalie says I'll talk to a lamppost. So where are you?
A: Basingstoke. I clean on the wards at the hospital. Early shifts.
B: Ah, respect. Proper hard work, that. Honestly. When I first came over, I did nights in care homes. Years. Nobody looks at you, you know? You're just the one in the tabard. So I know that job is hard.
A: It can be like that. The patients notice you, though. The nurses do. Some of them know my name.
B: That's the thing, yeah. The old ones, they'd just want somebody to sit down for a minute.
A: They do. You have a little chat while you're doing their table. Sorry. What do you do now?
B: Electrician. Self-employed, in Gloucester. Rewires, kitchens. My van's outside, the heater's broken, so I'm freezing every morning. Hey, the lady I spoke to before, Alison, she told me her dog's called Biscuit.
A: Oh, I know! My cat's called Biscuit. We worked that out in the first one.
B: Two Biscuits! That's a sign. Of what, I don't know. Do you have kids?
A: Two, grown up. Kirsty's got a little boy, he's two. He's just started saying Nanny Jo.
B: Ahh, Nanny Jo! That's lovely, man.
A: I have him on my days off. He's into everything. Sorry, I'm going on.
B: No, go on! I've got Kai, my partner's boy, he's thirteen. He eats everything in the fridge and grows out of his boots every two months. Third pair this year.
A: Liam was like that. He's in Reading now. Twenty-five. I still think he's about twelve.
B: They're always twelve, you know. My mum's in Zimbabwe, I'm forty and she still asks if I'm eating properly.
A: Are you?
B: Ha! Meal deal from the Co-op. So no. But on Sunday I make sadza, beef stew. Kai loves it now. First time, he looked at it like it was, er, like it was wallpaper paste.
A: I don't know what that is, sorry.
B: Like a thick maize porridge, you eat it with your hands with the stew. Proper comfort food.
A: Oh, that sounds nice. I'm not very adventurous. Shepherd's pie, spag bol. A roast on Sundays.
B: A roast is perfect, man. Nothing wrong with that. Hey, did you see the car park prices, at hospitals? I did a job at one, I paid nine pound.
A: They've gone up again for us as well. Staff. It's not right.
B: That's not right, no. You're there cleaning for them —
A: That's what I said to Gary.
